questions.question: A shopkeeper has a box of 18 apples. He wants to pack them into bags, with 3 apples in each bag. How many bags will he need?

options.explanation: 3 bags would only hold 9 apples, which is less than 18.
5 bags would hold 15 apples, which is less than 18.
6 bags will hold exactly 18 apples (3 apples per bag).
18 bags would hold 54 apples, which is more than needed.

questions.explanation: To find out how many bags are needed, we can count in groups of 3 or use repeated subtraction: 18 - 3 = 15 (1 bag), 15 - 3 = 12 (2 bags), 12 - 3 = 9 (3 bags), 9 - 3 = 6 (4 bags), 6 - 3 = 3 (5 bags), 3 - 3 = 0 (6 bags). So, he will need 6 bags.
questions.hint: Divide the total number of apples by the number of apples per bag.
